headline: Approved amendment to July 15 minutes; discussed trail markers, maintenance, memorial bench requests, and environmental libraries.
summary: Members approved a correction to the July 15th, 2026 minutes, 6-0. They also discussed proposed environmental libraries, trail mileage markers, trail maintenance, and memorial bench requests, without other votes.
decisions: Approved amendment to the July 15th, 2026 minutes, changing the previous meeting date to June 2, 2026, 6-0.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Farmington Canal Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, September 1, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER   
 The meeting was called to order by Chair Commissioner D. Schaefer at 7:10 PM. 
2. ATTENDANCE   
 The Clerk called the roll, and the following members were present: 
 
Present: 
 
Commissioner David Schaefer, Chairman 
Commissioner Nick Hansen 
Commissioner Peter Cyr 
Commissioner Kathy Larson 
Commissioner Jeffrey Campbell 
Commissioner Gerry Tobin 
 
Also in attendance were Eugene Lipschutz, Town Planner; Briana J. Belton-Robinson, 
Boards and Commissions Clerk; and 2 members of the public, Norm B. and Mike 
Melanson, who attended virtually. 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 Chairman D. Schaefer requested a motion to adopt the minutes from Wednesday, July 
15th, 2026, with amendments. 
 
Please see the corrections approved for amendment: 
Chairman D. Schaefer noted one correction: under the section titled “Approval of Previous 
Meeting Minutes,” the minutes should identify the previous meeting as June 2, 2026. 
 
Commissioner P. Cyr made the motion to amend the previous agenda, and Commissioner 
J. Campbell seconded it. 
 
Vote by Roll Call: 
 
Yes 
Commissioner David Schaefer, Chairman 
Commissioner Nick Hansen 
Commissioner Peter Cyr
Commissioner Kathy Larson 
Commissioner Jeffrey Campbell 
Commissioner Gerry Tobin 
 
No 
 
Absent 
 
The motion passed. 
 
• Roll Call Vote Summary: Yes 6, No 0, Abstentions 0, Absent 0 
  
4. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 Chairman D. Schaefer opened the floor for public comment. 
 
Norm B. stated that he had no public comment. 
 
Mike Melanson stated that he had no public comment. 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.   
 Chairman D. Schaefer reported receiving correspondence from someone affiliated with the 
University of Connecticut about a high school student interested in installing environmental 
libraries along the Farmington Canal Trail. The proposed libraries would allow trail users to 
take, exchange, and contribute environmentally focused publications. 
 
Commissioner P. Cyr volunteered to follow up regarding the proposal and asked about 
funding and the Town approval process. 
 
Eugene Lipschutz, Town Planner, stated that the proposal involved installing an 
improvement on the trail and recommended coordinating with the Public Works 
Department. He explained that the project could require a referral to the Planning and 
Zoning Commission as a municipal improvement before ultimately receiving Legislative 
Council approval. Commissioner P. Cyr agreed to connect the project representatives with 
E. Lipschutz and Public Works Director Joe Colello. 
 
Commissioner N. Hansen expressed support for the concept but raised concerns regarding 
long-term maintenance and ensuring that the environmental library would not become an 
unmanaged repository for unwanted materials. He also recommended developing a 
clearer, publicly accessible process for individuals seeking to install benches, signs, 
libraries, or other trail improvements. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer noted that a written procedure already exists for memorial benches,
including Commission review of locations. E. Lipschutz explained that municipal 
improvements generally follow a process involving Town departments, Planning and 
Zoning review, and Legislative Council approval. He offered to outline the process for the 
Commission. 
 
Commissioner G. Tobin also raised concerns regarding responsibility for future 
maintenance of the proposed environmental libraries. Chairman D. Schaefer agreed that 
the Commission would need to address maintenance before approving any proposal. 
 
Commissioner J. Campbell supported making installation procedures more visible and 
accessible on the Commission's webpage. 
 
Mike Melanson stated that he recently assisted an individual seeking information about 
donating a memorial bench and that the individual had difficulty determining whom to 
contact. E. Lipschutz clarified that bench requests should go to the Planning and Zoning 
Department and said the webpage could make contact information clearer. 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No Executive Session was held. 
7. REPORTS   
 
 
  1. Report of the Chairman  
  E. Lipschutz reported that Commissioner J. Campbell had forwarded information 
regarding erosion along the trail. The concern was forwarded to Engineering and 
Public Works for review and follow-up. 
 
Commissioner N. Hansen reported receiving an analysis from Mike Melanson 
regarding the painted mileage markers along the trail. The analysis identified 
approximately 46 existing markers in varying conditions and approximately 49 missing 
markers. Commissioner N. Hansen agreed to forward the information to E. Lipschutz 
and Public Works Director J. Colello. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer explained that Public Works originally painted the mileage 
markers, and Commission volunteers subsequently maintained them using materials 
supplied by Public Works. He noted that Public Works still has the stencils. 
 
Commissioner K. Larson said she and another former Commission member repainted 
the markers several years ago. She explained that repainting had been delayed 
because of plans for a larger trail-wide mileage marking system extending from south 
to north. 
 
Commissioner P. Cyr reported that he contacted State Representative Sweet 
regarding proposed trail signage and questions concerning trail naming and branding. 
He stated that the applicable bond request or package had not yet been located. 
Norm B. agreed to provide Commissioner P. Cyr with information regarding the 
funding source or bond package.
Commissioner J. Campbell noted that the trail already includes branding associated 
with the East Coast Greenway and other statewide trail systems. He said this 
precedent would help maintain Hamden's identity while also recognizing the trail as 
part of a larger regional system. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer supported consistent mileage references along the trail 
beginning at the New Haven border while maintaining the Farmington Canal Trail's 
existing name and identity. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer asked E. Lipschutz for information on maintenance work 
completed by Public Works during the summer and whether capital funds were used. 
E. Lipschutz stated that he did not have an update but would follow up with Public 
Works for the next meeting. 
 
Commissioner P. Cyr recommended that the Commission develop an updated, 
consolidated list of trail maintenance and capital needs before the upcoming budget 
season. He said such a document would give the new administration a clear 
understanding of the Commission's priorities and show the impact of deferred 
maintenance. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer supported the recommendation and referenced a previous 
trail-wide assessment conducted with the Mayor, Public Works, Planning, 
Engineering, and Commission members. He noted that the prior assessment 
identified numerous projects, including bridge repairs, stone dust replacement, 
fencing, root damage, and other maintenance needs. Some projects had been 
completed, but many remained outstanding. 
 
E. Lipschutz agreed to look for previous assessments and grant materials and said he 
would also contact the Town's Grants Director about an earlier Recreational Trails 
Grant application. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer and Commissioner J. Campbell discussed deteriorating 
wooden infrastructure and signage along portions of the trail. Commissioner J. 
Campbell specifically identified deteriorating bridge planks, a patched bridge area with 
an additional opening, deteriorating fencing and railings, and a damaged sign near 
River Road. 
 
Commissioner K. Larson identified Tom Brown of the Parks Department as the 
individual familiar with trail maintenance and the potential repainting of mileage 
markers. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer suggested that one or more Commission members conduct a 
trail walk with T. Brown to inventory maintenance needs. Commissioner J. Campbell 
volunteered to participate. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer stated that he would confirm the appropriate Town contact and 
explore arranging the trail inventory. E. Lipschutz recommended including Public 
Works Director J. Colello in communications. 
8. OLD BUSINESS
Commissioner J. Campbell asked about access to the Commission's general email 
account. 
 
B. Belton-Robinson stated that she and Chairman D. Schaefer currently have access to the 
Commission email account. Chairman D. Schaefer explained that because messages 
cannot automatically be forwarded outside the Town's email system, he would periodically 
check the account. B. Belton-Robinson stated that she could also forward messages to 
Chairman D. Schaefer as they are received. 
 
B. Belton-Robinson identified an August 17, 2026 email from Jennifer Tucker regarding a 
request to memorialize a friend's son along the trail. Mike Melanson clarified that the 
correspondence concerned the memorial bench request discussed earlier in the meeting, 
specifically a bench with a memorial plaque. 
 
E. Lipschutz requested that the correspondence be forwarded to him so that Planning and 
Zoning staff could provide the applicant with information regarding the established process. 
 
Commissioner J. Campbell asked whether another Commissioner could also be provided 
access to the Commission's general email account. B. Belton-Robinson stated that she 
would inquire with Town Clerk Karimah Mickens regarding whether additional 
Commissioners could receive access and, if permitted, the process for doing so. 
9. NEW BUSINESS   
 Commissioner J. Campbell informed the Commission of an upcoming linear trail 
conference scheduled at Southern Connecticut State University on October 2, 2026. He 
stated that he would be unable to attend and asked whether another Commissioner 
planned to participate. 
 
Commissioner P. Cyr indicated that he had the conference on his calendar. Commissioner 
J. Campbell agreed to provide additional information regarding the event. 
 
B. Belton-Robinson confirmed that the Commission's next meetings were scheduled for 
Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at 7:00 PM and Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 7:00 PM. 
 
Chairman D. Schaefer said he could not attend the October 6 meeting and asked whether 
another Commissioner would be willing to convene it in his absence. 
 
Commissioner N. Hansen volunteered to convene the October 6, 2026 meeting. 
10. ADJOURNMENT   
 Commissioner P. Cyr made a motion to adjourn. Commissioner K. Larson seconded the 
motion. 
 
The motion passed unanimously. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:58 PM.
